svg.title: The Cedar FieldLink Gateway: a custom connector for an Azure Function
svg.desc: Top path, user requests. Lina uses an app, a flow or the dispatch agent, which calls the custom connector Cedar FieldLink Gateway. The connector uses OAuth 2.0 with Microsoft Entra ID: client app cedar-gateway-connector, single tenant, signing in with the connector's managed identity instead of a client secret, resource api://cedar-fieldlink-gateway, delegated scope Sla.Read. The request reaches the function app func-cedar-fieldlink-dev. First App Service authentication validates the token: audience, issuer, allowed client; without a valid token it answers HTTP 401 before any code runs. Then the function SubcontractorSla reads X-MS-CLIENT-PRINCIPAL, requires the scope Sla.Read (403 otherwise), validates subcontractor and dates (400), and calls FieldLinkApi. FieldLinkApi obtains a FieldLink token with the client credentials grant, using Cedar's server client and the secret from Key Vault through a Key Vault reference read with the app's managed identity, and calls GET /v2/reports/jobs; the function returns the SLA summary. Bottom path, outbound events: the queue fieldlink-outbound, filled by the lesson 90 webhook and the lesson 91 topic consumer, triggers DeliverOutbound, which posts the contract message to FieldLink /v2/events with the message id as idempotency key. 2xx: delivered. 400, 409, 422: a record on fieldlink-outbound-rejected. No answer, 401 after one token refresh, 403, 404, 429 or 5xx: the function throws, the queue retries, and after the maximum dequeue count the message moves to fieldlink-outbound-poison for replay in lesson 96. Excluded paths keep the lesson 90 endpoints, which authenticate with an HMAC signature and a function key, reachable without an Entra token.
svg.text: User requests: connector → Entra token → function → FieldLink with server credentials
token valid? else 401, no code runs
Outbound events: queue → function → FieldLink, with replayable failures
fieldlink-outbound-rejected: kept for people, not retried
fieldlink-outbound-poison: after max dequeue count → lesson 96
Why a function, not the connector, holds the FieldLink server credential
Custom connectors do not support the client credentials grant. The function keeps it in Key Vault and exposes only what Cedar
decides (SLA figures, no job details), to users who hold Sla.Read. App Service authentication covers the whole app, so the
lesson 90 endpoints are listed as excluded paths: they prove the caller with an HMAC signature and a function key instead.
The connector's managed identity replaces a client secret: one federated credential per environment after import.
